info.name: Zameens — Razorpay Checkout & AI Quota (UI-impacting changes)
info.description: Focused collection covering only what changed for the Razorpay redirect-checkout rework and the new AI monthly-question quota. Every request here either has a different request/response shape than before, or introduces new client-facing behavior the frontend has not built against yet. Companion doc: docs/razorpay-client-integration-guide.md (full narrative walkthrough + the /payments/result page spec). Set accessToken after OTP verification; adminAccessToken needs an ADMIN-role user for the Commerce Admin folder.

item.name: Auth (get a token to use below)
Verify OTP → copy accessToken into the collection variable
List plans
item.description:
UI CHANGE NEEDED:
1. Each plan now returns `productId` — this is what you must send to POST /orders, NOT the plan's own `id`. This field did not exist before; if the UI was hardcoding or reverse-mapping a product id, remove that workaround.
2. Each plan now returns `billingMode`: "ONE_TIME" or "RECURRING". Only show a purchase CTA for ONE_TIME plans right now — RECURRING plans have no working purchase flow yet (POST /orders will reject them with 409 PLAN_REQUIRES_SUBSCRIPTION). Hide or disable the buy button for RECURRING plans, or show a "coming soon" state.
3. Each plan now returns `aiMonthlyQuota` (integer or null=unlimited) — if the plans/pricing page shows feature comparisons, this is the live source of truth for the AI question limit per plan, not a hardcoded number in the frontend.

item.name: List services
item.description: UI CHANGE NEEDED: each service now returns `productId` (new field) — required for POST /orders when purchasing this service. The service's own `id` is only for POST /service-requests, not for ordering.

item.name: 2. Checkout — the new redirect flow (UI change: full rebuild)
(Service purchase only) Create service request first
item.description: Unchanged endpoint, but now sits in front of a checkout: keep the returned `id` — it becomes `targetId` in the order below. Skip this step entirely for plans and promotions.

item.name: Create order — Plan
item.description: UI CHANGE NEEDED: for a plan, send only productId/quantity — no targetType/targetId. New rejection to handle: 409 PLAN_REQUIRES_SUBSCRIPTION if the plan's billingMode is RECURRING (see the List Plans note).

item.name: Create order — Promotion (boost a listing)
item.description:
UI CHANGE NEEDED: `targetType` must be the literal string "LISTING" (previously free text — anything else is now rejected with 400). `targetId` must be a listing the logged-in user owns, or the order is rejected with 409 TARGET_NOT_OWNED — the UI should only ever offer this action from the seller's own listing management screen, never let a listing id be typed in freely.

Note: there is currently no public endpoint to discover promotion products (their productId/price/type) — confirm with backend how this screen sources that catalog before building it.

item.name: Create order — Paid service
item.description: UI CHANGE NEEDED: `targetType` must be the literal string "SERVICE_REQUEST". `targetId` is the ServiceRequest id from the step above — it must belong to the current user and be unpaid, or this is rejected with 409 SERVICE_REQUEST_NOT_PAYABLE.

item.name: Create payment — returns a redirect URL, not a checkout payload
item.description:
BREAKING UI CHANGE — this is the core of the rework:

OLD contract (no longer exists): response had `checkoutPayload` + `providerPublicKey`; the client loaded Razorpay Checkout.js and opened a modal with them.

NEW contract: response is only `{ paymentId, provider, redirectUrl }`.

Required frontend changes:
1. DELETE any Razorpay Checkout.js `<script>` tag / SDK import — it is never used.
2. DELETE any `new Razorpay(options).open()` modal code.
3. DELETE any client-side payment-success handler that called POST /payments/verify — that endpoint has been removed entirely, calling it now 404s.
4. ADD: on receiving this response, do a full-page navigation — `window.location.href = redirectUrl` — not a popup, not an iframe.
5. `returnUrl` is no longer an accepted field on this request (silently ignored if sent) — the redirect target is fixed by the server via COMMERCE_RETURN_BASE_URL, not per-request.

item.name: GET /orders/{orderId} — poll this after redirect, don't trust the URL alone
item.description: Unchanged endpoint, but now load-bearing for the new flow: after the customer is redirected back to your /payments/result page, use this to confirm `status: "PAID"` rather than trusting the `?status=` query param alone for anything business-critical (e.g. don't unlock a feature purely because the URL said success).

item.name: 3. Reference only — never called by the client directly
Payment callback (Razorpay redirects the BROWSER here)
item.description:
NEW endpoint. The frontend never fetches this with XHR/fetch — Razorpay's hosted checkout page redirects the customer's browser here after payment, and this endpoint itself responds with an HTTP redirect (302) onward to `{frontend}/payments/result?orderId=...&status=...`.

The ONLY thing the frontend needs to build for this is the landing page at `/payments/result`, reading `orderId` and `status` from its own query string. See docs/razorpay-client-integration-guide.md section 5 for the full table of `status` values (success / pending / invalid / passthrough Razorpay statuses) and what to render for each — in particular the `pending` case, where the UI must poll GET /orders/{orderId} rather than assume failure.

item.name: Payment webhook (server-to-server, Razorpay → our server)
item.description: No UI relevance at all — included only so backend/QA can exercise it. The frontend should never call this.

item.name: 4. Commerce Admin — plan management (UI change: new fields)
Admin: Create plan
item.description:
UI CHANGE NEEDED for the admin panel's plan editor: two new fields to add to the form.
- `billingMode`: "ONE_TIME" or "RECURRING" (defaults to ONE_TIME if omitted). Note RECURRING plans currently cannot actually be purchased by customers (Section 2) — the admin UI should probably warn about this until subscriptions ship.
- `aiMonthlyQuota`: integer, or omit/null for unlimited AI Property Assistant questions per month on this plan.

item.name: Admin: Update plan (toggle billingMode / change AI quota)
item.description: Changing billingMode or aiMonthlyQuota only affects future purchases/usage windows — it does not retroactively alter a customer's already-granted entitlement or already-counted usage this month.

item.name: 5. AI Assistant — monthly quota (UI change: new error to handle)
Create conversation
item.description: Unchanged. Does not itself consume any AI quota — creating a conversation (even with an initialQuery) generates no AI response and costs nothing.

item.name: Send message (SSE) — can now return AI_MONTHLY_QUOTA_EXCEEDED
item.description:
UI CHANGE NEEDED. This is a Server-Sent Events response (Postman will show raw event lines, not a normal JSON body — that's expected, this endpoint is unchanged in transport). What's new is a possible event:

  event: error
  data: {"error":{"code":"AI_MONTHLY_QUOTA_EXCEEDED","message":"You have used all 5 AI Property Assistant questions included in your plan this month."}}

The frontend's SSE `error` event handler must recognize `AI_MONTHLY_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` specifically and show a clear "you've used your monthly AI questions, upgrade your plan" message (ideally linking to the pricing page) rather than a generic error toast. This is on the same SSE error channel already used for AI_CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE etc., so if that channel is already handled generically, this is a new *code* to special-case, not a new *mechanism* to build.

Quota resets on the calendar month and only counts questions that were actually answered — a rejected attempt never counts against it, so retrying after upgrading works immediately.
